newsitem.title: SPAIN: Utilities, banks push Madrid stocks to new high.
newsitem.headline: Utilities, banks push Madrid stocks to new high.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed at a new high on Monday, bouyed by interest in the electric utility sector and in selected banks amid third quarter results.
The general index rose 2.40 points, 0.63 percent, to 383.22 and the Ibex added 25.24 points, 0.58 percent, to 4,402.61.
Banking group BBV rose 90 pesetas to 5,330 after announcing net attributable profit of 70.45 billion pesetas for the nine months to September, released just before the close.
Argentaria bank added 120 pesetas to 5,330 after today's dividend payment. Santander also rallied ahead of this week's results announcement.

But electric firms were still at the forefront amid recently announced changes in corporate structure and speculation of more to come. Endesa rose 10 pesetas to 8,220, and Fenosa climbed 25 pesetas to 889.

Trade in other electric firms Viesgo, Nansa and Hidrocantabrico was suspended after press reports that the latter was seeking to buy the former two companies from Endesa. Endesa later denied the report, but speculation of similar moves continue to drive sector shares, dealers said.
Volume, boosted by the extra interest in electricity shares, was around 47 billion pesetas.
